title: The Wavering Centre

patient.name: Mdm Letchumy d/o Arumugam
patient.presenting_complaint: Straight lines appear wavy and central vision in left eye has deteriorated over 3 weeks

history.hpc: Mdm Letchumy noticed 3 weeks ago that the edges of doorframes looked wavy when she covered her right eye. She has also noticed a blurry patch in the centre of her vision in the left eye, making reading difficult. She denies any pain, redness, or flashing lights. Her right eye vision has been slowly reducing over the past 2 years but she thought it was 'just old age'. She had a routine Amsler grid check at a community screening which was abnormal, prompting referral.
history.family_hx: Elder sister has 'macular problems' and required eye injections
history.social_hx: Lives alone, no smoking history, does not drive, enjoys reading and sewing

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Early nuclear sclerosis bilaterally, pseudophakic right eye (previous cataract surgery)

fundus.right: Large confluent soft drusen in macula, geographic atrophy involving foveal centre — dry AMD
fundus.left: Large soft drusen, subretinal greyish-green membrane with surrounding subretinal fluid and small subretinal haemorrhage at fovea — consistent with choroidal neovascular membrane (CNV)

investigations.oct_macula: Left: subretinal hyperreflective material (type 2 CNV), intraretinal fluid, subretinal fluid — centre-involving neovascular AMD. Right: photoreceptor loss at fovea with outer retinal atrophy — geographic atrophy.
investigations.fundus_fluorescein_angiography: Left: early hyperfluorescence with late leakage from CNV membrane, classic pattern
investigations.amsler_grid: Left: marked central distortion and scotoma. Right: mild distortion.

diagnosis: Neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration, left eye. Geographic atrophy (dry AMD), right eye.

immediate: Urgent intravitreal anti-VEGF injection to left eye — ranibizumab 0.5mg or aflibercept 2mg
Treat-and-extend protocol: monthly anti-VEGF until fluid resolves, then extend interval by 2 weeks
Amsler grid given to patient — monitor daily at home, present urgently if new distortion
Right eye: no treatment for geographic atrophy — monitor, low vision aids referral
follow_up: Left eye: monthly OCT and anti-VEGF as per treat-and-extend, minimum 3 loading doses
Target: absence of intraretinal and subretinal fluid on OCT
Right eye: 6-monthly review, AREDS2 supplements (lutein, zeaxanthin, zinc, vitamins C/E) to slow progression
Low vision rehabilitation referral for both eyes
patient_education: Wet AMD is treatable with injections — early treatment preserves vision, does not restore what is lost
Injections are given into the eye under topical anaesthesia — reassure patient about procedure
Daily Amsler grid self-monitoring is essential — any new distortion requires urgent review within 24 hours
AREDS2 supplements recommended for the unaffected eye to slow dry AMD progression
Smoking cessation strongly recommended — smoking doubles AMD risk

key_points: Elicits metamorphopsia (wavy/distorted lines) — hallmark of CNV
Asks about central scotoma vs peripheral vision preservation
Asks which eye is worse and time course of each
Requests OCT macula — gold standard for fluid and CNV detection
FFA to characterise CNV type and leakage pattern
Examines fellow eye for drusen load and risk of conversion
Identifies wet (neovascular) AMD in left eye — not just AMD
Distinguishes wet vs dry AMD between eyes
Identifies choroidal neovascularisation as the acute threat
Urgent anti-VEGF injection to left eye
Amsler grid for home monitoring and safety-netting
